newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK contender says misrule to fuel democracy urge.
newsitem.headline: HK contender says misrule to fuel democracy urge.

text.p: A candidate for Hong Kong's leadership after the British colony reverts to China next year has said the public's demand for democracy will grow if post-colonial rulers fail to provide good government.

"The pace of democracy depends on how people feel about their safety, their family and the feeling of free choice and so forth," Peter Woo, a prominent businessman and public health care overseer, said in an interview published on Wednesday.
"All these things will then bring out a public view: maybe we need more democracy to safeguard these matters," Woo told the English-language daily South China Morning Post.
"The cornerstone of my policy platform is based on a personal feeling about the need to feel safe and free. That's what I think most Hong Kong people want," he said.
Woo, 50, is among five candidates so far in the race to become Chief Executive after Britain pulls out in 265 days, ending more than 150 years of colonial rule.
The successor to Governor Chris Patten will be designated next month by a 400-member China-controlled Selection Committee.

There is no public election but candidates are trying to impress the public because China has said the future leader must be acceptable to Hong Kong people. A steady flow of pulse-taking polls tracks the candidates' popularity.

Woo came third in a South China Morning Post poll last week with 9.5 percent public support, behind former Chief Justice Sir Ti Liang Yang, who scored 45 percent, and shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa, who clocked up 24 percent.

Woo is honorary chairman of one of Hong Kong's biggest conglomerates, Wharf (Holdings) Ltd, and a member of a China-appointed body tackling the 1997 handover. He also heads Hong Kong's Hospital Authority.
The democracy issue has stirred controversy over the past year as China vowed to scrap Hong Kong's elected Legislative Council and water down a Bill of Rights introduced by Patten.
